contraindications: Valproate in women of childbearing potential: major teratogen (neural tube defects, neurodevelopmental disorders); avoid unless no alternative exists.
interactions: Fosphenytoin or phenytoin + combined oral contraceptive: CYP3A4 induction lowers ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel exposure; contraceptive failure; use additional contraception.
Levetiracetam + combined oral contraceptive, acyclovir or methylprednisolone: no clinically relevant pharmacokinetic interaction.
Acyclovir + ibuprofen: additive nephrotoxicity; avoid NSAIDs, keep well hydrated and dose acyclovir by renal function.
IVIG + combined oral contraceptive (estrogen): additive thrombotic risk; consider withholding the estrogen-containing pill during IVIG.
Lacosamide: dose-related PR prolongation; obtain an ECG before IV loading.
output.proposed: Lorazepam, a second-line antiseizure medication (levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, valproate or lacosamide), IV acyclovir, IV methylprednisolone and IVIG with ibuprofen and a combined oral contraceptive

output.query: Autoimmune encephalitis presenting with status epilepticus: evaluation and first-line treatment

results.finding: Possible autoimmune encephalitis can be recognized from subacute memory, psychiatric or seizure features with MRI, CSF or EEG support, before antibody results are available.
Acyclovir is started on suspicion of HSV encephalitis without waiting for the PCR result.

In a cohort of 577 patients with antibody-mediated encephalitis of the NMDA receptor type, early first-line immunotherapy (steroids, IVIG or plasma exchange) and tumor removal when present were associated with better outcomes; second-line agents were used when first-line therapy failed.
Levetiracetam, fosphenytoin and valproate were equally effective second-line agents for benzodiazepine-refractory status epilepticus.

output.summary: Autoimmune encephalitis can be recognized clinically, with MRI, CSF and EEG support, before antibody results [Graus_2016], while acyclovir covers HSV encephalitis until it is excluded [Tunkel_2008]. Early first-line immunotherapy and removal of an associated tumor are associated with better outcomes [Titulaer_2013]. Status epilepticus is treated with a benzodiazepine and a second-line agent [ESETT_2019].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: WBC 13.2, CRP 28.4, ESR 72, procalcitonin 0.8, lactate 2.4; electrolytes, renal and hepatic function normal; toxicology screen negative; beta-hCG negative
action_criteria.label: Emergency laboratory work-up: glucose, CBC, electrolytes, magnesium, renal and hepatic function, toxicology screen, beta-hCG
action_criteria.rationale: Glucose, electrolyte, renal and hepatic derangements are reversible causes of seizures and decide the ASM and its dose; a toxicology screen because new psychosis with seizures has no evident cause, and beta-hCG because she is of reproductive age [Brophy_2012].

action_criteria.rationale: Fever with tachycardia and procalcitonin 0.8 makes systemic or CNS bacterial infection a question until cultures and CSF answer it [Brophy_2012].

action_criteria.label: Non-contrast head CT after stabilization
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes hemorrhage, mass or edema that would change management, and must precede any LP [Brophy_2012].

action_criteria.rationale: Persistent impaired consciousness after a seizure, with abnormal movements of uncertain nature, needs EEG confirmation of non-convulsive SE; continuous monitoring for at least 24 hours [Brophy_2012]; terminology [ACNS_2021].

action_criteria.label: MRI brain with gadolinium for encephalitis
action_criteria.rationale: New-onset status epilepticus with fever and psychiatric features needs MRI for encephalitis and other causes [Brophy_2012; Graus_2016].

action_criteria.rationale: Febrile encephalitis with seizures needs CSF for infection and for neuronal antibodies; CSF NMDAR IgG is more sensitive than serum [Tunkel_2008; Graus_2016].

action_criteria.label: Serum autoimmune encephalitis antibody panel including NMDAR IgG (cell-based assay)
action_criteria.rationale: Serum and CSF neuronal antibodies are tested together when autoimmune encephalitis is possible [Graus_2016].

action_criteria.rationale: A young woman with anti-NMDAR encephalitis is screened for an ovarian teratoma, preferably with MRI or ultrasound [Titulaer_2013].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Levetiracetam has no relevant interaction; fosphenytoin lowers contraceptive levels; ibuprofen adds to acyclovir nephrotoxicity; valproate is avoided

action_criteria.rationale: No interaction in the case changes the ASM choice; the check covers contraceptive induction, NSAID nephrotoxicity with acyclovir and valproate teratogenicity [ESETT_2019].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on autoimmune encephalitis criteria, first-line immunotherapy and tumor removal
action_criteria.label: Literature: autoimmune encephalitis with status epilepticus, immunotherapy and tumor removal
action_criteria.rationale: General evidence only; not a clinical step in the pathway.

prohibited_recommendations: Do NOT give haloperidol or other neuroleptics for agitation: neuroleptics worsen anti-NMDAR encephalitis and risk neuroleptic malignant syndrome; use benzodiazepines.
Do NOT defer the lumbar puncture once CT excludes mass effect: CSF NMDAR antibody is the most sensitive test.
Do NOT delay teratoma removal once identified: the tumor is the immunogenic source.
required_recommendations: Give a benzodiazepine now: IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg (maximum 4 mg per dose, repeat once), or IM midazolam 10 mg without IV access [Glauser_2016].
Start IV acyclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours, adjusted for renal function, on suspicion of HSV encephalitis, and stop it once HSV PCR is negative and the alternative diagnosis is secure [Tunkel_2008].
Load a second-line ASM: levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV (maximum 4500 mg), and avoid valproate because she is of reproductive age and valproate is a major teratogen [ESETT_2019].
Continue video-EEG for at least 24 hours after clinical and electrographic seizure control [Brophy_2012].

Start first-line immunotherapy once infection is reasonably excluded, without waiting for every antibody result: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days with IVIG 0.4 g/kg daily for 5 days or plasma exchange [Titulaer_2013; Graus_2016].
Arrange removal of the right ovarian teratoma with gynecology as soon as she is stable [Titulaer_2013].

avoided_actions.rationale: Autonomic instability is monitored at the bedside in ICU; ambulatory Holter not indicated acutely.
Neuropsychological battery cannot be performed in encephalopathic patient and does not change acute management.

key_clinical_evidence: Young woman with new-onset seizures + psychiatric features + autonomic instability + fever = consider anti-NMDAR encephalitis until proven otherwise
CSF NMDAR antibody is more sensitive than serum; both should be sent
An ovarian teratoma is found in about half of women aged 18 to 45 with anti-NMDAR encephalitis; its removal with immunotherapy improves outcome [Titulaer_2013]
MRI is normal in most patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis; a normal MRI does not exclude the diagnosis
Extreme delta brush is a characteristic EEG pattern of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; dyskinesias without an EEG correlate are not seizures

patient.history_present_illness: A 34-year-old White female graphic designer was brought by EMS to the emergency department after her roommate found her having a brief generalized seizure lasting 2 minutes and called 911. The roommate reports the patient had been unwell for 5 days with progressively worsening headache, confusion, and behavioral changes: she was talking to herself, becoming paranoid, and at one point undressing in the living room. She had reduced oral intake for 3 days. The roommate noted the patient had no history of seizures. On EMS arrival, the patient was minimally responsive, combative, with a temperature of 39.1°C measured by EMS. In the ED she is markedly agitated, requiring soft restraints, not following commands, with disorganized speech, and responding to internal stimuli (appears to be hallucinating). The patient wore a medic alert bracelet that says 'no known allergies.'
